030package dev.visdb.seesaw.datasources.products;
031
032import java.sql.Connection;
033import java.sql.DatabaseMetaData;
034
035import dev.visdb.seesaw.datasources.DbSupport;
036
037/**
038 * Should be at least one of these for a supported database. It creates a
039 * {@link DbSupport} that works with the database specified by the
040 * DatabaseMetaData.
041 * These are placed in {@code META-INF} using an annotation like
042 * {@snippet lang="java":
043 * @ServiceProvider(path="SS/DbSupport/H2", service=DbSupportCreator.class)
044 * }
045 * Note in this example that {@code dbMeta.getDatabaseProductName().equals("H2")}.
046 * <p>
047 * Any {@code DbSupportCreator}s found are tried in order.
048 * The first creator that matches the metadata returns non null, the search
049 * is terminated and that value is returned.
050 * Normally {@code position} is not used with the annotation, but if there are
051 * multiple creators that match, it's use might be needed.
052 * <a href="https://bits.netbeans.org/dev/javadoc/org-openide-util-lookup/org/openide/util/lookup/ServiceProvider.html">
053 * See @ServiceProvider javadoc</a>.
054 */
055public interface DbSupportCreator {
056  /**
057   * Create a DbSupport for the connection. The DatabaseMetaData belongs
058   * to the connection; use to refer to dbMeta productVersion or ...
059   * If this creator can't construct a DbSupport for the meta data return null;
060   *
061   * @param sharedConnection
062   * @param dbMeta
063   * @return may be null
064   */
065  DbSupport create(Connection sharedConnection, DatabaseMetaData dbMeta);
066}
